title: concert poster , logo designing
desc:
The task is to turn our upcoming music concert into something people can’t scroll past. I need a striking advertising poster, polished photos, and a short, high-energy promo video that all work together under one visual theme.  

Here’s the scope I have in mind:  
• Poster – A3 print-ready and web versions, bold typography, clear date/venue, and space for sponsor logos.  
• Photo edits – Retouch and colour-grade the artist shots so they drop straight into the poster and our socials.  
• Promo video – 30-60 seconds, cut from the raw clips I’ll supply, synced to the headline track, ending on the event details.  

Everything should carry the same look and feel so our audience recognises the concert instantly, whether they see it on a street wall, Instagram story, or YouTube ad. I’ll share brand colours, fonts, and footage as soon as we start.  

Delivery deadline: any time within the next month, but the sooner the better so we can start the ad run. Source files (PSD/AI, Lightroom presets, Premiere/After Effects project) should be included with the finals.  

If this sounds like your kind of creative sprint, let’s make some noise.

Deliverables  
• Live multi-camera (or single-camera if you’re confident) coverage of the entrance, streamed to the in-hall screen/projector in HD or better, with backup recording for later use.  
• Final edited “pre-dance tribute” video, 3–5 minutes long, colour-graded, mixed with the romantic track, delivered in MP4 (1080p) and a web-ready version.  
• All raw footage transferred to us on a drive or secure download link within a week of the event.

Acceptance Criteria  
• Zero noticeable lag or dropouts on the live stream.  
• Tribute video approved after one round of minor tweaks.  
• Audio levels balanced for both live stream and edited video.

title: Precise PDF-to-Docs Transcription
desc:
I have a short PDF of roughly 540 words that must be reproduced in Google Docs exactly as it appears now. Every word, line break, and piece of basic formatting (bold, italics, paragraph spacing) needs to carry over so the final document mirrors the source—no additions, omissions, or typos.

What I will share:
• The original PDF file.  
• A blank Google Docs link with edit permission.

What I need back:
• The Google Docs file populated with the text, accurately transferred.  
• A quick note confirming you have double-checked the word count and formatting.

Because the content is text-only, no image handling is involved. A keen eye for detail and a clean copy-and-paste workflow using a PDF reader and Google Docs will keep this simple yet precise. If you can finish promptly without sacrificing accuracy, that’s all I ask.

title: Customize Nano/Micro MDM Deployment Policies
desc:
I run a Linux-based instance of both nanoMDM and microMDM and I need a developer who can dive into their configuration layer to fine-tune software-deployment policies. My main goal is to enforce granular permissions management—who can install what, when, and under which conditions—across enrolled Apple devices without disrupting the existing enrollment workflow.

You will be working directly on the Linux host, updating configuration files and, when necessary, adjusting the Go code behind nanoMDM/microMDM to expose the policy controls I need. Expect to handle token-based authentication, profile signing, and the overall packaging pipeline so that newly approved apps propagate automatically while anything outside the policy is silently blocked.

Deliverables
• Updated nanoMDM/microMDM configs (or patched source) reflecting the new permissions rules  
• A short, repeatable script or Ansible role to apply the changes on fresh servers  
• Verification report showing successful deployment and denial scenarios on at least two test devices

Acceptance Criteria
The final setup must push approved software with no manual touches, log any blocked attempts, and survive a full system reboot on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.

If you have recent experience bending nanoMDM or microMDM to your will—and you’re comfortable debugging on Linux—let’s get started.

The finished video should flow smoothly, use text overlays to highlight key points, and feature background music that supports the learning mood without distracting viewers.

title: SEO partner to take full ownership of my site’s visibility
desc:
I need a seasoned SEO partner to take full ownership of my site’s visibility and drive it to higher positions on Google. The goal is clear: improve organic rankings across the board, and I’m looking for complete support—on-page, off-page, and technical.

• Off-page SEO: authority link building through white-hat outreach, digital PR, and backlink profile cleanup.  
• Technical SEO: full audit, page-speed fixes, Core Web Vitals tuning, mobile and crawl-ability improvements, and structured data validation via Google Search Console.

Acceptance criteria  
1. A baseline and follow-up ranking report that proves measurable gains for agreed-upon target keywords.  
2. A technical audit document listing issues, actions taken, and post-fix validation.  
3. Monthly performance summary from Google Analytics and Search Console showing organic growth.

You will have access to the CMS, Analytics, and Search Console. Please outline your proposed workflow, tools you rely on (e.g., Screaming Frog, Ahrefs, SEMrush), and realistic timelines for the first visible ranking lift.

title: Need USA Accounting Leads
desc:

  – Company name & website

Acceptance criteria  
• Minimum 95 % email validity when checked through ZeroBounce or a similar tool

title: Guest Speaker Release Contract
desc:
I already drafted a release agreement with AI for six guest speakers who appear in my forthcoming book and companion online course. Now I need a lawyer-grade version that a publishing house can rely on without hesitation..... using what I have developed as a starting point to minimise work of freelancer and ensuring all main points are covered

Scope  
• One clear, comprehensive contract that secures worldwide, perpetual permission to use each guest’s video, audio and transcript excerpts in every format (print, e-book, audiobook, streaming course, translations, etc.).  
• Language that makes it obvious the material may sit behind a paid course wall—the fee only covers production, hosting and day-to-day platform costs, not profit.  
• Explicit confirmation that we may edit or condense the interviews for the book while keeping the full recordings in the course.  
• Clauses on intellectual-property ownership, moral rights waivers, publicity rights, indemnification and governing law, drafted to conventional publishing standards.  

Acceptance criteria  
1. Final document delivered in editable Word format.  
2. Read-through version with plain-English comments explaining each clause.  
3. Ready for signature with space for six individual names or a template merge field.  

If you have publishing-sector contract experience and can turn this around quickly, I’d love to put the finishing touches on this project with you.

title: .NET E-Commerce Backend Optimization
desc:
Our live e-commerce site is built on the Microsoft .NET stack and, while feature-complete, the backend has begun to drag under load. Pages that once rendered in under a second now spike past five, occasional time-outs appear in the logs, and CPU usage sits uncomfortably high. I’m looking for help focused strictly on bug fixes and ongoing maintenance, with the immediate priority being performance bottlenecks on the server side.

You’ll start by profiling the application (IIS, ASP.NET MVC / Web API, Entity Framework, SQL Server) to pinpoint slow spots—inefficient queries, memory leaks, or blocking calls. From there, I need clean, well-commented patches that restore sub-second response times under typical traffic and remain stable in our staging environment for at least 48 hours before deployment.

Deliverables  
• Diagnostic report outlining root causes and performance metrics before/after fixes  
• Refactored .NET code and updated database scripts where required  
• A concise hand-off note describing changes, new settings (caching, connection pooling, etc.), and any monitoring recommendations

Acceptance criteria  
• Average backend response ≤ 1 s on 95% of requests under current load  
• No new exceptions introduced in Application Insights for 72 hours post-deploy  
• All existing unit tests pass; any new tests you add included in solution

If you have solid experience squeezing every millisecond out of .NET e-commerce apps, let’s talk.

Deliverables

desc:

desc:
Our production datalake pipeline on Hadoop is misbehaving: Spark and Flink jobs crash intermittently, completed stages fail to commit their results to the Hive tables, and overall throughput has slowed to a crawl. Acceptance criteria – once you are done:  
• All scheduled Spark and Flink jobs finish successfully when triggered manually and by the scheduler.  
• Output partitions appear in the target Hive table with correct row counts on at least two consecutive test runs.  
• End-to-end execution time returns to normal (or faster) baseline and remains stable for 48 hours of monitoring.

Deliverables

title: AI-Driven Commodity Intelligence Tool Development
desc:
For Project 40648634 - AI Commodity Intelligence Platform
